rationale: The workflow already applies the supported dependency-cache optimization (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE): it caches npm via actions/setup-node with cache: 'npm' keyed to izanami-frontend/package-lock.json, and caches coursier/sbt dependencies via coursier/cache-action@v6, matching the cache pattern whose measured example (batch-hirumi-pattern-bat-1ac2203839ed8c07-r2) added exactly this kind of lockfile-keyed node cache. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (measured example batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508, 26.8% elapsed savings with a 5-minute job timeout) is not safely applicable here: CI history shows successful runs take roughly 8-13 minutes, so a binding timeout risks killing valid slow runs and breaking build/test coverage, while the measured 5-minute example is for a much lighter check workflow; a non-binding timeout would save nothing. No matrix exists for P-LIT-FAIL-FAST/P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST, and path-filter or test-selection patterns would reduce required coverage. No supported, safe change is available.
